# XY Forever serial protocol 1.27: session commands

Part of the [XY Forever serial protocol 1.27](../PROTOCOL.md).

### 0x01 `hello`

Greet the device; required before any other command. Answers in every state. While searching for the device, a tool may send `hello` every 0.5 s on the open
port until a reply with status ok arrives. The reply tells the tool what the device supports: the protocol version, the release version and image it runs, the
limits and the commands it answers. 1.1 added the keys from `mode` on (and `build`, replaced in 1.15 by `version` and `image`); a device without `cmds` is a
pre-v1 device (see the rules).

Request: empty (the device ignores any payload).

| Reply field, after the status (1 to 256 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `info` | text ASCII, 1..256 B | ASCII, `XYF1` and then `key=value` items, separated by `;`; no NUL; at most `max_hello` bytes. The keys are listed below; tools ignore keys they do not know. |

On an error: the status only. Errors: none of its own. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `text`). Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.1.

#### `hello` keys

The `hello` text: `XYF1`, then these keys in this order, each as `;key=value`. A build's text never changes while it runs, except `stage2` and the stage-2
command's bit of `cmds`: both are set before the reply to the first `hello` of a boot when stage 2 loads, and cleared again if stage 2 stops answering as it
should; and (1.23) `confirm`, once the device has read its settings and when Ask before USB control is saved, and `trust`, as the question is asked and
answered; and (1.25) `serial`, as USB mode is picked. Tools ignore keys they do not know and must not rely on the order.

| Key | Since | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `service` | 1.0 | `usb`: the service that answers |
| `role` | 1.0 | `b`: the processor that answers |
| `proto` | 1.0 | `1.27`: protocol version `MAJOR.MINOR` (pre-v1 devices: `1`) |
| `install` | 1.0 | `stock-88a06a7e`: the boot-partition writer `boot.install` uses (the stock bootloader's own, at 0x88a06a7e) |
| `version` | 1.15 | XY Forever release version `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (`0.1.0` the first); builds between two releases carry the same one |
| `image` | 1.15 | the os.ldr this boot runs: the first 8 lowercase hex digits of its SHA-256, which name its build (`builds/<image>/`). The device hashes the image the stock bootloader read from the boot partition, however it was installed (`boot.install` or the dev menu), once per boot, before its first `hello` reply; `unknown` when no XY Forever image is there to hash |
| `mode` | 1.1 | build mode (`product`, the only mode with this service) |
| `payload` | 1.1 | `4160`: `max_payload` |
| `read` | 1.1 | `1024`: `max_read` |
| `stage` | 1.1 | `7340032`: `max_stage` |
| `cmds` | 1.1 | the request types this build answers: 32 lowercase hex digits, a 128-bit number written most significant digit first, in which bit t (value 2^t) is set when type t is answered (Python: `int(cmds, 16) >> t & 1`). Derived from each command's build switch when the build is compiled; the stage-2 command's bit is set at run time while stage 2 is loaded |
| `dev` | 1.1 | `1` when the build answers developer commands; absent otherwise |
| `confirm` | 1.23 | Ask before USB control (Settings): `1` when the first command but `hello` of a connection makes the device ask "Allow this computer to control your OP-XY?" (`trust`), `0` when every command runs at once. No USB command changes it, only the device's Settings row with its own keys; file transfers (MTP, the serial file commands) stay open and can replace or delete `settings.txt` like any file; `1` until the device has read its settings (the default when it has none) |
| `trust` | 1.23 | the question's state on this connection: `none` (not asked: the setting is off, or no command but `hello` came yet), `asking` (every command but `hello` answers `waiting`), `allowed` (the user allowed: commands run), `refused` (the user did not: every command but `hello` answers `declined`). An answer lasts until the USB cable is unplugged (seen as a USB bus reset; closing and reopening the port keeps it) or the device restarts; on the stock serial fallback (no composite) the device sees no unplug, so until it restarts |
| `serial` | 1.25 | USB mode (Settings) for serial: `on`, or `off` when it is MTP: then every command but `hello` answers `serial_off` and tools show "Serial is off on your OP-XY: Settings > USB mode". The USB device always carries both MTP and serial; the mode switches each in place (with Serial, MTP sessions are refused), the moment it is picked, never re-enumerating |
| `stage2` | 1.6 | the loaded stage 2's version, decimal; `0` when none is loaded (no file, or it failed a check). Always the last key |

The product build answers (220 bytes):

```text
XYF1;service=usb;role=b;proto=1.27;install=stock-88a06a7e;version=0.1.0;image=f458e3cc;mode=product;payload=4160;read=1024;stage=7340032;cmds=000000000000fffb001700031fff00be;dev=1;confirm=1;trust=none;serial=on;stage2=0
```

### 0x03 `file.read`

Read a file, whole (at most 4096 bytes) or a range. Two forms: with `offset` and `length` (ranged), or the path alone (whole file, `too_large` above 4096
bytes). Use the ranged form: whole-file replies above 1 KiB hung the device in tests. To read any file, read ranges of `max_read` bytes from offset 0 until a
reply holds fewer. An offset at or past the end of the file is ok with no data; `range` means the device's seek to the offset failed. A malformed path is
`bad_request`; a well-formed one that the device's file policy refuses (a control byte) is `refused`.

| Request field (10 to 248 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path under `/yaffs2/`, NUL-terminated; no empty, `.` or `..` parts; no control bytes |
| `offset` | u32 | Optional. First byte to read |
| `length` | u32 | Optional. Bytes to read, at most `max_read` (1..1024) |

| Reply field, after the status (0 to 4096 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | rest, 0..4096 B | ranged form: up to `length` bytes, fewer only at the end of the file; whole form: the whole file |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `range`, `too_large`. The reply never gains fields (it ends in
`rest`). Tool timeout: 15 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x04 `screen.read`

Read part of the display framebuffer (screenshot). Reads memory only. The framebuffer is 245760 (0x3C000) bytes: 480 columns, stored right to left, of 256
RGB565 pixels each, top to bottom; the visible picture is the first 216 pixels of each column. A screenshot reads offsets 0, 1024, 2048, ... until it has 245760
bytes. A request that is not exactly 4 bytes, an offset past the end or no valid framebuffer gives `range`.

| Request field (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `offset` | u32 | byte offset into the framebuffer (0..245759) |

| Reply field, after the status (5 to 1028 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `framebuffer` | u32 | the framebuffer's address (informational; also sent with `range`) |
| `pixels` | rest, 1..1024 B | up to `max_read` bytes from `offset` |

On an error: the status and `framebuffer`. Errors: `range`. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `rest`). Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.
